headline: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana 2.0
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana 2.0

Building a Skilled and Self-Reliant Workforce

24 SEP 2026 10:47AM by PIB Delhi

Equipping rural youth with relevant skills and access to employment opportunities is central to advancing inclusive and sustainable rural transformation. To advance this goal, the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) was launched on 25 September 2014 under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission. Building on this, the DDU-GKY 2.0 scheme is currently being implemented across 31 States and Union Territories through over 749 approved projects, with more than 760 active training centers and over 455 Project Implementing Agencies, covering all sectors of the economy as on date. Since inception in 2014-15, more than 18.47 lakh candidates have been trained for more than 800 job roles, and over 12.43 lakh have been placed. Complementing the skilling efforts, RSETIs promote self-employment and rural entrepreneurship. As of date, 647 RSETIs across 634 districts have trained 63.47 lakh candidates, with 45.60 lakh successfully settled. These initiatives strengthen industry-aligned training, digital delivery, employment retention, and sustainable livelihood opportunities for rural youth.

Strengthening Rural Youth through Skills and Opportunities

India’s young population presents a significant opportunity to strengthen economic growth and rural livelihoods. The youth population is projected to reach nearly 345 million by 2036. Harnessing this demographic potential requires greater access to quality skills, employment, and livelihood opportunities.

Recognizing this need, the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) launched the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) on 25 September 2014, under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission. As DDU-GKY marks its 12th anniversary this year, the programme continues to strengthen pathways from skills to employment and sustainable livelihoods for rural youth. For more than a decade, the scheme has been providing placement-linked skill training to rural youth aged 15-35 years from poor households.

It also promotes social inclusion through mandatory coverage of SC/ST communities (50%), women (33%), and persons with disabilities (5%). Over the past decade, the scheme has evolved to place greater emphasis on employment outcomes and post-placement support. The Government notified the upgraded DDU-GKY 2.0 Guidelines in May 2025, strengthening the framework around training, placements, employment sustainability, and post-placement support. The revised framework provides training across multiple sectors based on industry requirements, including aerospace and aviation, agriculture, beauty and wellness, green jobs, healthcare, textiles, and others. The continued focus on rural skilling is also reflected in the Union Budget 2026–27, which has allocated ₹750 crore to DDU-GKY.

Special Initiatives: Targeted Interventions for Vulnerable Regions

Two special programmes are being implemented under DDU-GKY 2.0:

Roshni: It addresses the specific needs of Left-Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected districts notified by the Ministry of Home Affairs. It mandates residential skill training, with 40% coverage for women candidates. The initiative has been extended to Aspirational Districts, focusing on local infrastructure, education, health, natural resources, and traditional skills.

Himayat: It is a special DDU-GKY scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. It covers rural and urban youth, including BPL and APL persons, and supports wage, self, and gig employment. The scheme is 100% centrally funded and implemented with State support through dedicated Mission Management Units.

North East: Acknowledging the challenges in terms of socio-cultural differences and topography unique to the North Eastern States, out of the total allocation for DDU-GKY, 10% is earmarked for the North-Eastern States.

Hard to reach Areas: Further there is provision for Special Area Allowance where Project implementing agencies shall be eligible for a payment at the rate of an additional 10% of the Base training cost per candidate.

DDU-GKY 2.0: A Shift Towards Sustainable Employment

DDU-GKY 2.0 adopts a more end-to-end approach to skilling and employment, covering the journey from training and placement to employment retention and career progression.

The revised framework strengthens training standards, extends the minimum placement duration, and enhances post-placement support. It also addresses the challenges associated with migration and strengthens technology-enabled monitoring and implementation.

Standardising Training Framework

DDU-GKY 2.0 retains the 576-hour minimum while providing a more structured training framework. A three-month course comprises 396 hours of domain training and 180 hours of mandatory non-domain training. The non-domain component is standardised across four areas: English Communication (60 hours), Employability and Life Skills (60 hours), Computer and Digital Literacy (30 hours), and Entrepreneurship (30 hours). It ensures that candidates receive job-specific technical skills alongside communication, workplace, digital, and entrepreneurial capabilities.

Placement Duration

Earlier, DDU-GKY placement was defined as continuous employment for a minimum of three months. Building on this stronger training foundation, under DDU-GKY 2.0, the minimum placement duration has been extended to six months. The revised guidelines cover both continuous and non-continuous employment, including wage, self-employment, and gig employment.

Job Melas for Connecting Rural Youth with Employers

Job Melas are organised by SRLMs at the block and Gram Panchayat levels to connect local youth with potential employers. They include youth registration and counselling, employer verification, and tracking of placement outcomes for one year through Kaushal Panjee. The Melas are mainly for youth with employable skills, including DDU-GKY-trained candidates seeking better job opportunities. Funding of up to ₹50,000 per GP-level fair and ₹1 lakh per block-level fair is available from the DDU-GKY budget, subject to placement of 100 and 200 candidates, respectively.

Strengthening Employment Retention and Career Progression

Under DDU-GKY 2.0, greater emphasis has been placed on sustained employment. To support the extended six-month placement duration, DDU-GKY 2.0 provides 12 months of post-placement tracking to facilitate employment continuity, specifically:

Placed candidates receive financial assistance of ₹7,620, at ₹1,270 per month for six months.

In addition, retention support of ₹5,000 per candidate is provided to candidates who remain employed for 365 days, with a maximum employment break of 60 days.

Placed candidates are also provided with upskilling and reskilling opportunities after 12 months of placement, enabling them to strengthen their skills and improve their prospects for continued employment and career progression.

Migration Support Centres (MSC)

Given that a considerable proportion of trained candidates migrate in search of livelihood opportunities, DDU-GKY 2.0 has placed renewed emphasis on strengthening migration support systems. State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs) establish Migration Support Centres (MSCs) in areas with a high concentration of placed candidates. These centres operate both within the home state and in destination states. MSCs offer a range of services to support candidates during this transition, including accommodation assistance, counselling, and placement support.

They also facilitate the flow of employment-related information, encourage alumni networking, and strengthen engagement with employers. Beyond this, the centres liaise with local administrative bodies and service providers to help candidates settle into urban work environments and remain in stable employment over time. Reflecting the growing importance of this support system, per-centre annual funding for MSCs has been increased considerably, from ₹10 lakh earlier to as much as ₹30 lakh under the revised framework.

Employing Technology in Implementation

Technology integration has been a defining feature of DDU-GKY since its inception. The framework relies on geo-tagged and time-stamped biometric attendance records, computer labs, and e-learning facilities. These measures strengthened programme monitoring while enhancing trainees' exposure to digital tools.

DDU-GKY 2.0 builds upon this technological foundation by introducing an end-to-end digital solution encompassing the entire programme lifecycle. The platform spans PIA onboarding, project submission and evaluation, training-centre and candidate management, assessment and certification, financial management, and project monitoring and placement tracking.

The revised approach also introduces:

Advanced dashboards for real-time programme monitoring.

Public candidate portal for training search and viewing PIA performance ratings.

Automated processes, including Project Registration Number (PRN) generation, grievance redressal, and certificate verification.

Digital attendance and assessment through face authentication and real-time dashboards.

Skill India Digital Hub integration for automated course-detail validation.

Leading the Rollout (2025-26) of DDU-GKY 2.0

Goa has emerged as the pioneer in creating batches of DDU GKY 2.0.

Andhra Pradesh has commenced training of more than 12000 candidates in a short span of 3 months.

Jammu & Kashmir allocated 100% targets allocated and commenced trainings for 91% of the allocation.

Key Milestones Achieved Under the Scheme

DDU-GKY is currently being implemented across 31 States & Union Territories through an extensive skilling network. As on date, the programme has 749 approved projects, with 760 active training centres, in partnership with more than 455 PIAs.

Since its inception in 2014-15, DDU-GKY has trained over 18.47 lakh candidates, covering all 36 sectors of the economy and over 800 job roles, and placed over 12.43 lakh. This reflects the scheme’s wide sectoral reach and focus on industry-aligned skill development for rural youth.

Over 9.71 lakh women were trained, and over 6.34 lakh women secured placements under the scheme.

Other Initiatives Supporting Rural Youth Entrepreneurship

While DDU-GKY focuses on placement-linked wage employment, the Government has simultaneously strengthened self-employment and entrepreneurship pathways through Rural Self-Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs). The programme provides free residential training to rural unemployed youth aged 18-50 years, followed by handholding support for setting up sustainable livelihoods. The programme creates dedicated skill infrastructure in every district of the country. It focuses on upskilling rural youth, especially those from below poverty line (BPL) and DAY-NRLM households.

As on date, a total of 647 RSETIs are operational across 634 districts in 33 States/UTs. Since its inception (2009), the scheme has trained 63.47 lakh candidates. Total of 45.60 lakh candidates have also been settled. Among the candidates settled under RSETI, around 94% have established sustainable self-employment ventures. About 6% have secured wage employment.

Shaping Rural India’s Workforce for the Future

Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Files to Freedom: DEPwD Sets the Stage to Turn Pendency into Productivity and Waste into Resource

24 SEP 2026 10:29AM by PIB Delhi

From clearing pending matters to reclaiming office space, from digitizing records to responsibly disposing of e-waste, the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) is gearing up to make Special Campaign 6.0 a focused drive for cleaner workplaces, faster disposal of pendency and more efficient governance. The campaign, being undertaken from 2nd to 31st October 2026, will give special emphasis to the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste, while institutionalizing Swachhata across the Department and its organizations.

Launched by the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG), Special Campaign 6.0 seeks to institutionalize Swachhata and minimize pendency in Government offices. The campaign is being implemented in two phases, with the Preparatory Phase from 16th to 30th September 2026, followed by the Implementation Phase from 2nd to 31st October 2026.

DEPwD has already put in place the institutional mechanism for the campaign. A Nodal Officer has been nominated for the Department, while all Subordinate and Attached Offices, Public Sector Undertakings and Autonomous Bodies under the administrative control of DEPwD have been advised to nominate their respective Nodal Officers and identify pending matters in accordance with the parameters prescribed by DARPG.

The Department is building on the momentum generated during Special Campaign 5.0, held from 2nd to 31st October 2025, when DEPwD and its organizations achieved the targets set for the campaign. During the month-long drive, 11,972 physical files/documents were digitized and weeded out, approximately 15,588 square feet of office space was freed, and revenue of ₹14,47,619 was generated. As many as 64 cleanliness campaigns, covering indoor and outdoor spaces, were also organized by the Department and its organizations across the country.

The effort, however, did not end with the conclusion of the campaign. In keeping with the guidelines of DARPG, DEPwD and its organizations have continued to undertake Swachhata and pendency-reduction activities every month since November 2025. The achievements have also been regularly uploaded on the Special Campaign 6.0 Portal (SCDPM), reflecting the Department’s emphasis on sustained action rather than a one-time cleanliness exercise.

Special Campaign 6.0 will further reinforce this approach by bringing together the twin objectives of Swachhata and good governance—reducing avoidable pendency, improving record management, freeing up usable space and ensuring responsible disposal of obsolete material, particularly e-waste. The campaign will seek to convert idle records, redundant material and pending matters into opportunities for greater efficiency, accountability and productivity.

DEPwD is committed to making Special Campaign 6.0 a meaningful and outcome-oriented exercise. Concerted efforts will be undertaken by the Department and its organizations to achieve the targets identified during the preparatory phase and to carry forward the culture of cleanliness, timely disposal and efficient use of public resources as an integral part of everyday governance.

headline: PBSHABD
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

Prasar Bharati's Trusted News for India’s Newsrooms

24 SEP 2026 10:13AM by PIB Delhi

PBSHABD is the free news feed service of Prasar Bharati, India's public service broadcaster. Launched in March 2024, it serves as a news wire for the wider media industry. Registered organisations may draw text, video, audio, photographs and infographics in 15 Indian languages. The service is free up to March 2027 and serves 3,600 media organisations. Its content is gathered through a nationwide network and verified through multiple layers of editorial checks. PBSHABD thereby extends the reach of credible information across India's media landscape.

From PBNS to PBSHABD: Evolution of a Public News Service

Prasar Bharati is India's public service broadcaster and an autonomous body created by an Act of Parliament. It came into existence on 23 November 1997 under the Prasar Bharati Act, 1990. The corporation works through two constituents, Akashvani and Doordarshan. Its mandate is a fair and balanced flow of information in the public interest.

News gathering has always been central to this mandate. The Prasar Bharati News Service (PBNS) began as a news wire strictly for the broadcaster's own editorial teams. Its copy and feeds supported bulletins across Akashvani and Doordarshan. At that stage, the service remained an internal newsroom resource.

The scope of the service was enlarged in March 2024. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB) launched PBSHABD on 13 March 2024 in New Delhi. The service now carries the name Prasar Bharati – Shared Audio-Visuals for Broadcast and Dissemination. It gives registered media organisations free, ready-to-use news in text, video, audio, photo and infographic formats. An internal news wire thus became an open multimedia news-sharing platform. The table below traces the main milestones of this journey.

Year | Milestone

1990 | Parliament enacts the Prasar Bharati Act.

1997 | The corporation comes into existence on 23 November 1997.

Till 2024 | PBNS works as an internal news wire for Prasar Bharati's editorial teams.

March 2024 | PBSHABD is launched on 13 March as a free, multi-format news-sharing platform.

March 2025 | Free access is extended to March 2026 on completion of one year.

March 2026 | Free access is extended further, up to March 2027.

Ahead | PBSHABD 2.0 is planned, with new product lines and improved delivery.

PBSHABD is not a newsroom built from scratch. It is an extension of news infrastructure developed over several decades. The same correspondents, desks and bureaux now serve a far wider set of users. The reach of the content has changed, while the editorial foundation has stayed the same. How that reach works is best understood through the design of the service itself.

Did You Know? The name of the service carries two meanings. It expands to Shared Audio-Visuals for Broadcast and Dissemination. In Hindi, the word shabd means the spoken or written word. The platform was built to share that word widely, quickly and free of cost.

PBSHABD: A Multi-Format, Multilingual News Feed

PBSHABD is a news feed service of Prasar Bharati, open to media users round the clock. It supplies timely, authentic and ready-to-use news content from India and the world. The feed carries developments as they occur, from the national capital to district headquarters.

Its users are registered media organisations, digital publishers and content creators. Newspapers, news television channels and digital news publishers form the bulk of this base. In two years of operation, the service has built a user base of 3,600 media organisations.

Content is offered in five formats, namely text, video, audio, photographs and infographics. News is provided in 15 Indian languages and under nearly 50 news categories. Coverage extends across national, regional and local developments. The service is free of cost. Registered users pay no subscription fee for the content they download. Free access has been assured up to March 2027. Read More About Features & Benefits of PBSHABD

Who can register

Registered newspapers and journals may sign up with a valid RNI certificate. Television and radio stations require valid uplink and downlink certificates. Digital publishers may register on submission of a copy of their PAN. Each organisation receives one login, which its journalists mayshare within the newsroom. Read more about PBSHABD registration here.

One Platform, Many Content Products

PBSHABD is designed as a bouquet of services rather than a single news wire. Each product is prepared for direct use by a particular kind of newsroom.

One feature sets the platform apart from a conventional news agency. Content carries no Prasar Bharati logo and needs no credit line. A small newspaper may therefore run a national story under its own masthead.

From the Ground to the Newsroom: The Network Behind PBSHABD

The strength of PBSHABD lies in the network that feeds it. Prasar Bharati runs one of the largest news gathering and desk networks in the country. More than 1,500 reporters, correspondents and stringers contribute to this pipeline. Sixty dedicated edit desks work round the clock on the material they send. Akashvani and Doordarshan run their own regional news units and bulletin services. Between them, they cover almost every State and Union Territory. The table below indicates the reach of this network.

Network | Reach on the ground

Akashvani News | 46 Regional News Units, 1 Headquarter 607 bulletins a day in 92 languages and dialects

Doordarshan News | 31 Regional News Units, 1 Headquarter Over 145 bulletins in more than 22 languages and dialects

Field strength | Over 1,500 reporters, correspondents and stringers across the country

Editorial desks | 60 dedicated desks working round the clock

Editorial checks before dissemination

News on PBSHABD passes through multiple layers of editorial checks. The service maintains firm guardrails against fake, morphed or manipulated content. It is careful with material drawn from unverified online sources. Every story is timestamped, datelined and properly captioned. Users therefore know exactly when and where a development took place. Technology widens the reach of this service. The news gathering and editorial network gives it a strong news foundation.

Accuracy, Authenticity and Timeliness: The Spirit of Public Service

Accuracy and authenticity sit at the centre of the service. Content is professionally produced, edited and verified before it is shared. The round-the-clock feed ensures that verified news reaches users without delay. Its range of formats and languages makes the service genuinely inclusive. In a crowded information environment, verified content is itself a public good.

Connecting India's Diverse Media Ecosystem

Audiences now receive news across many platforms at the same time. Television, newspapers, websites, mobile applications, YouTube and social media all carry the day's events. A newsroom must therefore publish in several formats every single day. PBSHABD connects Prasar Bharati's news gathering infrastructure with this wider ecosystem. Newspapers, television broadcasters, digital publishers, creators and platforms draw from the same feed.

The benefit is sharpest for smaller and regional organisations. A district newspaper rarely maintains correspondents in Delhi or abroad. Through PBSHABD it can access professionally produced national and international coverage. Ready-to-use text, video and audio reduce both cost and turnaround time.

PBSHABD carries Prasar Bharati's news gathering capability beyond its own channels. Credible information now travels through thousands of independent outlets. The service is positioned for steady expansion in the period ahead. Free access to the platform has been extended up to March 2027. Media organisations may therefore plan their use of the feed with certainty. The user base has risen to 3,600 media organisations in two years of operation.

Accurate news remains a public good in an age of rapid information flows. Prasar Bharati remains committed to free, fair and factual news reporting and dissemination. Every verified story on the platform strengthens the foundation of an informed citizenry. PBSHABD thus stands as shared national infrastructure for the dissemination of credible information.
